benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Eased to about $102.81 on 9 Oct (Trading Economics), down roughly 1.4% from $104.28 the prior day, as President Trump said the US will not strike Iran before November's midterm elections, even as Gulf of Mexico shut-ins deepened to 63% of oil output ahead of Hurricane Isaias. Week-ago is the 2 Oct value from this site's own prior run.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: Eased to $3.12 on 9 Oct (Trading Economics), down about 1.5% on the day after five straight sessions of gains. Week-ago is the 2 Oct value from this site's own prior run; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price is largely insulated.

note: Brent and WTI eased about 1-1.5% on 9 Oct after President Trump said the US will not strike Iran before November's midterm elections, even as Gulf of Mexico shut-ins deepened to 63% of oil output ahead of Hurricane Isaias's landfall and a tanker was hit off Qatar, west of the usual Hormuz attack cluster. TTF and Henry Hub also eased.
